bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷一 梁本紀第一: 太祖上
title.raw: 卷一 梁本紀第一: 太祖上 Volume 1 Later Liang Annals 1: Taizu 1

sentences.zh: 新五代史卷一 梁本紀第一

translations.literal: New History of the Five Dynasties, Volume 1 — Basic Annals of Liang, Part One.
translations.idiomatic: New History of the Five Dynasties, Volume 1: Basic Annals of Liang, Part One.

sentences.zh: 太祖神武元聖孝皇帝，姓硃氏，宋州碭山午溝里人也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, divine in martial prowess, sagely and filial in virtue, bore the surname Zhu; he was a native of Wugou Village in Dangshan, Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor—martial, sagely, and filial—was of the Zhu clan, from Wugou Village in Dangshan, Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 其父誠，以《五經》教授鄉里，生三子，曰全昱、存、溫。

translations.literal: His father Cheng taught the Five Classics in the district and had three sons, named Quanyu, Cun, and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng made a living teaching the Five Classics locally. He had three sons: Quanyu, Cun, and Wen.

sentences.zh: 誠卒，三子貧，不能為生，與其母傭食蕭縣人劉崇家。

translations.literal: When Cheng died, the three sons were poor and could not support themselves; with their mother they hired themselves out for food to Liu Chong of Xiao County.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng died the brothers were destitute. They and their mother went to work for their board in the household of Liu Chong of Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 全昱無他材能，然為人頗長者。

translations.literal: Quanyu had no other talent, yet as a man he was quite respectable.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyu had little ability, but he was a man of decent character.

sentences.zh: 存、溫勇有力，而溫尤兇悍。

translations.literal: Cun and Wen were brave and strong, and Wen was especially fierce and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Cun and Wen were strong and bold; Wen was the more brutal of the two.

sentences.zh: 唐僖宗乾符四年，黃巢起曹、濮，存、溫亡入賊中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Qianfu era of Emperor Xizong of Tang, Huang Chao rose in Cao and Pu; Cun and Wen fled into the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianfu (877), under Emperor Xizong of Tang, Huang Chao rebelled in Cao and Pu prefectures. Cun and Wen joined his ranks.

sentences.zh: 巢攻嶺南，存戰死。

translations.literal: When Chao attacked Lingnan, Cun died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign into Lingnan, Cun was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 巢陷京師，以溫為東南面行營先鋒使。

translations.literal: When Chao took the capital, he appointed Wen vanguard commander of the southeastern campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao seized Chang'an he made Wen commander of the vanguard for the southeastern expeditionary force.

sentences.zh: 攻陷同州，以為同州防禦使。

translations.literal: He captured Tong Prefecture and made Wen its defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tongzhou and installed Wen as its military governor.

sentences.zh: 是時，天子在蜀，諸鎮會兵討賊。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was in Shu, and the regional commanders were gathering troops to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had fled to Shu, and the military governors were mustering armies against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 溫數為河中王重榮所敗，屢請益兵於巢，巢中尉孟楷抑而不通。

translations.literal: Wen was repeatedly defeated by Wang Chongrong of Hezhong and repeatedly asked Chao for reinforcements, but Chao's chief steward Meng Kai blocked the requests and would not pass them on.
translations.idiomatic: Wen suffered repeated defeats at the hands of Wang Chongrong of Hezhong. He begged Chao for more troops, but Meng Kai, Chao's chief steward, suppressed every request.

sentences.zh: 溫客謝瞳說溫曰：「黃家起於草莽，幸唐衰亂，直投其隙而取之爾，非有功德興王之業也，此豈足與共成事哉！

translations.literal: Wen's retainer Xie Tong urged Wen, saying: "The Huang family rose from the wilds and, by fortune of Tang's disorder, simply thrust into a gap and seized power—they have no merit of founding a dynasty. How can they be worth sharing great undertakings with?
translations.idiomatic: Wen's adviser Xie Tong said to him: "The Huang clan came out of nowhere and only took the realm because Tang was collapsing. They have done nothing that deserves a throne. Why stay tied to them?

sentences.zh: 今天子在蜀，諸鎮之兵日集，以謀興復，是唐德未厭於人也。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is in Shu, and the armies of the provinces gather daily to plan restoration—Tang's mandate is not yet exhausted among the people.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor is in Shu, and provincial armies are assembling every day to restore the dynasty. The people have not yet given up on Tang.

sentences.zh: 且將軍力戰于外，而庸人制之於內，此章邯所以背秦而歸楚也。

translations.literal: Moreover, you fight hard abroad while mediocrities control you within—this is why Zhang Han turned his back on Qin and went over to Chu."
translations.idiomatic: "And you bleed for them in the field while fools run you from the rear—the same trap that drove Zhang Han to abandon Qin for Chu."

sentences.zh: 」溫以為然，乃殺其監軍嚴實，自歸於河中，因王重榮以降。

translations.literal: Wen thought it sound; he killed his army supervisor Yan Shi, returned to Hezhong on his own, and submitted through Wang Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wen agreed. He killed his army inspector Yan Shi, crossed back to Hezhong, and surrendered through Wang Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 都統王鐸承制拜溫左金吾衛大將軍、河中行營招討副使，天子賜溫名全忠。

translations.literal: The supreme commander Wang Duo, acting on imperial commission, appointed Wen Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and deputy campaign commander of Hezhong; the Son of Heaven granted Wen the name Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Wang Duo, by imperial order, made Wen grand general of the Left Golden Guard and deputy campaign commander in Hezhong. The court then gave him the name Quanzhong—"wholly loyal."

sentences.zh: 中和三年三月，拜全忠汴州刺史、宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Zhonghe, Quanzhong was appointed prefect of Bian and military governor of the Xuanwu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhonghe 3 (883), Quanzhong became prefect of Bianzhou and military governor of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 四月，諸鎮兵破巢，復京師，巢走藍田。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the allied armies broke Chao, recovered the capital, and Chao fled to Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the coalition routed Huang Chao, retook Chang'an, and drove him toward Lantian.

sentences.zh: 七月丁卯，全忠歸於宣武。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of the seventh month, Quanzhong returned to Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh month's dingmao day, Quanzhong went home to his Xuanwu base.

sentences.zh: 是歲，黃巢出藍田關，陷蔡州。

translations.literal: That year Huang Chao came out through Lantian Pass and took Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later that year Huang Chao broke out through Lantian Pass and seized Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使秦宗權叛附於巢，遂圍陳州。

translations.literal: The military governor Qin Zongquan rebelled and joined Chao, then besieged Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan, the local governor, defected to Chao and laid siege to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐州時溥為東南面行營兵馬都統，會東諸鎮兵以救陳。

translations.literal: Shi Pu of Xuzhou was overall commander of the southeastern campaign forces; he gathered the eastern provinces' troops to relieve Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu of Xuzhou held the title of overall commander for the southeast and called up eastern provinces to rescue Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳州刺史趙犨亦乞兵于全忠。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou, prefect of Chen, also begged Quanzhong for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's prefect Zhao Chou asked Quanzhong for help as well.

sentences.zh: 溥雖為都統而不親兵，四年，全忠乃自將救犨，率諸鎮兵擊敗巢將黃鄴、尚讓等。

translations.literal: Though Pu was overall commander he did not lead the troops in person; in the fourth year Quanzhong himself went to save Chou, leading the allied armies to defeat Chao's generals Huang Ye and Shang Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Pu held the supreme command but kept out of the field. In the fourth year Quanzhong marched in person to relieve Chou and, at the head of the coalition, smashed Huang Chao's lieutenants Huang Ye and Shang Rang.

sentences.zh: 犨以全忠為德，始附屬焉。

translations.literal: Chou, owing Quanzhong a debt of gratitude, began to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the rescue, Chou placed himself under Quanzhong's authority.

sentences.zh: 是時，河東李克用下兵太行，度河，出洛陽，與東兵會，擊巢。

translations.literal: At that time Li Keyong of Hedong marched down the Taihang, crossed the Yellow River, came out at Luoyang, joined the eastern armies, and struck at Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Hedong came down the Taihang range, crossed the river, advanced on Luoyang, and united with the eastern forces against Chao.

sentences.zh: 巢已敗去，全忠及克用追敗之於郾城。

translations.literal: Chao had already been beaten and fled; Quanzhong and Keyong pursued and defeated him again at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was already in retreat. Quanzhong and Keyong ran him down and beat him again at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 巢走中牟，又敗之于王滿。

translations.literal: Chao fled to Zhongmou and was defeated again at Wangman.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Zhongmou and suffered another defeat at Wangman.

sentences.zh: 巢走封丘，又大敗之。

translations.literal: Chao fled to Fengqiu and was routed once more.
translations.idiomatic: Pushed to Fengqiu, he was crushed again.

sentences.zh: 巢挺身東走，至泰山狼虎谷，為時溥追兵所殺。

translations.literal: Chao forced his way east to Langhugu on Mount Tai, where he was killed by Shi Pu's pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chao broke east to Langhugu Valley on Mount Tai, where Shi Pu's pursuit caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 九月，天子以全忠為檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事，封沛郡侯。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Son of Heaven made Quanzhong Honorary Grand Master of the Palace and co-equal with the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the court named Quanzhong honorary privy councilor and made him Marquis of Pei.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年三月，進爵王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Guangqi, his rank was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangqi 2 (886) he was raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 義成軍亂，逐其節度使安師儒，推牙將張驍為留後，師儒來奔，殺之。

translations.literal: The Yicheng army mutinied, drove out its military governor An Shiru, set the guard officer Zhang Xiao up as acting governor, and when Shiru came fleeing in, they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Troops of Yicheng mutinied, expelled governor An Shiru, and made a guard officer, Zhang Xiao, acting commander. When Shiru fled to them for refuge, they killed him.

sentences.zh: 遣硃珍、李唐賓陷滑州，以胡真為留後。

translations.literal: He sent Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin to take Hua Prefecture and installed Hu Zhen as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin to capture Huazhou and left Hu Zhen in charge there.

sentences.zh: 十二月，徙封吳興郡王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month his fief was moved to Prince of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month his title was shifted to Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 自黃巢死，秦宗權稱帝，陷陝、洛、懷、孟、唐、許、汝、鄭州，遣其將秦賢、盧瑭、張晊攻汴。

translations.literal: After Huang Chao's death, Qin Zongquan declared himself emperor and seized Shan, Luo, Huai, Meng, Tang, Xu, Ru, and Zheng prefectures, sending his generals Qin Xian, Lu Tang, and Zhang Zhi to attack Bian.
translations.idiomatic: With Huang Chao dead, Qin Zongquan crowned himself and overran Shan, Luoyang, Huai, Meng, Tang, Xu, Ru, and Zheng. He sent Qin Xian, Lu Tang, and Zhang Zhi against Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 賢軍板橋，晊軍北郊，瑭軍萬勝，環汴為三十六柵。

translations.literal: Xian camped at Banqiao, Zhi at the northern suburbs, and Tang at Wansheng; they ringed Bian with thirty-six stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Xian held Banqiao, Zhi the north suburbs, Tang Wansheng—thirty-six camps encircling Bian.

sentences.zh: 王顧兵少，不敢出。

translations.literal: Quanzhong had few troops and did not dare go out.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's forces were too weak to risk a sortie.

sentences.zh: 乃遣硃珍募兵於東方，而求救於兗、鄆。

translations.literal: He then sent Zhu Zhen to recruit troops in the east and asked Yan and Yun for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhu Zhen east to raise men and appealed to Yan and Yun prefectures for aid.

sentences.zh: 三年春，珍得萬人、馬數百匹以歸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, Zhen returned with ten thousand men and several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Zhen came back with ten thousand soldiers and hundreds of horses.

sentences.zh: 乃擊賢板橋，拔其四柵。

translations.literal: They then attacked Xian at Banqiao and took four of his stockades.
translations.idiomatic: They struck Xian at Banqiao and ripped out four camps.

sentences.zh: 又擊瑭萬勝，瑭敗，投水死。

translations.literal: They attacked Tang at Wansheng; Tang was defeated, threw himself into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Wansheng they routed Lu Tang, who drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 宗權聞瑭等敗，乃自將精兵數千，柵北郊。

translations.literal: When Zongquan heard that Tang and the others had been defeated, he personally led several thousand picked troops and stockaded at the northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Tang's defeat, Zongquan marched in person with an elite few thousand and fortified the north suburbs.

sentences.zh: 五月，兗州硃瑾、鄆州硃宣來赴援。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Zhu Jin of Yanzhou and Zhu Xuan of Yunzhou came with reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhu Jin of Yanzhou and Zhu Xuan of Yunzhou arrived to help.

sentences.zh: 王置酒軍中，中席，王陽起如廁，以輕兵出北門襲晊，而樂聲不輟。

translations.literal: The Prince set wine in camp; at mid-feast he feigned rising to use the privy, took light troops out the north gate to strike Zhi, and the music never stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince gave a banquet in camp. Midway through the feast he pretended to leave for the latrine, slipped out the north gate with a light force to hit Zhang Zhi, and the banquet music never missed a beat.

sentences.zh: 晊不意兵之至也，兗、鄆之兵又從而合擊，遂大敗之，斬首二萬餘級。

translations.literal: Zhi did not expect troops to arrive; the Yan and Yun armies closed from another side, and they were utterly defeated—more than twenty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was caught flat-footed. Jin and Xuan's men piled in from another angle. The slaughter topped twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 宗權與晊夜走，過鄭，屠其城而去。

translations.literal: Zongquan and Zhi fled by night; passing Zheng they sacked the city and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan and Zhi fled overnight, looting Zhengzhou on their way out.

sentences.zh: 宗權至蔡，復遣張晊攻汴。

translations.literal: Zongquan reached Cai and again sent Zhang Zhi to attack Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Cai, Zongquan sent Zhang Zhi against Bian once more.

sentences.zh: 王聞晊復來，登封禪寺後岡，望晊兵過，遣硃珍躡之，戒曰：「晊見吾兵必止。

translations.literal: When the Prince heard Zhi was coming again, he climbed the hill behind Fengchan Temple, watched Zhi's army pass, and sent Zhu Zhen to trail them, instructing him: "When Zhi sees our troops he is sure to halt.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Zhi was returning, the Prince took the ridge behind Fengchan Temple, watched the column go by, and sent Zhu Zhen to follow with orders: "Zhi will stop the moment he spots us.

sentences.zh: 望其止，當速返，毋與之鬥也。

translations.literal: When you see him stop, turn back at once—do not fight him."
translations.idiomatic: The instant he halts, wheel about. Do not engage."

sentences.zh: 」已而晊見珍在後，果止。

translations.literal: Presently Zhi saw Zhen behind him and indeed halted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi glanced back, saw Zhen, and stopped as predicted.

sentences.zh: 珍即馳還。

translations.literal: Zhen immediately galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen raced home.

sentences.zh: 王令珍引兵蔽大林，而自率精騎出其東，伏大塚間。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered Zhen to screen the great woods while he himself led picked cavalry out to the east and lay in ambush among the great mounds.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince hid Zhen in the timber while he took elite horsemen east to lie among the barrows.

sentences.zh: 晊止而食，食畢，拔旗幟，馳擊珍。

translations.literal: Zhi halted to eat; when they had finished eating they pulled up their banners and charged at Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi camped to eat, then struck his flags and rushed Zhen.

sentences.zh: 珍兵小卻，王引伏兵橫出，斷晊軍為三而擊之。

translations.literal: Zhen's troops gave ground slightly; the Prince led the ambush out sideways, cut Zhi's army in three, and struck it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's line bent back a little; then the Prince burst from cover, split Zhi's force in three, and hammered it.

sentences.zh: 晊大敗，脫身走。

translations.literal: Zhi was utterly defeated and escaped alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's army collapsed; he alone got away.

sentences.zh: 宗權怒，斬晊。

translations.literal: Zongquan in anger beheaded Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zongquan executed Zhi.

sentences.zh: 而河陽、陝、洛之兵為宗權守者，聞蔡精兵皆已殲於汴，因各潰去。

translations.literal: The troops of Heyang, Shan, and Luo who were holding cities for Zongquan, hearing that Cai's elite had all been destroyed at Bian, each broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons still loyal to Zongquan in Heyang, Shan, and Luoyang heard that his best troops had been wiped out at Bian and melted away.

sentences.zh: 故諸葛爽將李罕之取河陽、張全義取洛陽以來附。

translations.literal: Therefore Li Hanzhi, a general of Zhuge Shuang, took Heyang and Zhang Quanyi took Luoyang and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi, serving Zhuge Shuang, seized Heyang; Zhang Quanyi took Luoyang—both defected to the Prince.

sentences.zh: 十月，天子使來，賜王紀功碑。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Son of Heaven sent envoys granting the Prince a stele recording his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court sent a monument commemorating his victories.

sentences.zh: 硃宣、硃瑾兵助汴，已破宗權東歸，王移檄兗、鄆，誣其誘汴亡卒以東，乃發兵攻之，取其曹州、濮州。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin had aided Bian and, having broken Zongquan, were returning east; the Prince issued a proclamation to Yan and Yun falsely accusing them of luring Bian's deserters eastward, then sent troops against them and took Cao and Pu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After helping crush Zongquan, Xuan and Jin marched home. The Prince accused them—falsely—of recruiting his runaways and attacked, seizing Cao and Pu.

sentences.zh: 遂遣硃珍攻鄆州，大敗而還。

translations.literal: He then sent Zhu Zhen to attack Yun Prefecture, was badly beaten, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen's assault on Yunzhou failed disastrously.

sentences.zh: 十二月，天子使來，賜王鐵券及德政碑。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Son of Heaven sent envoys granting the Prince an iron certificate and a stele praising his virtuous government.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the court awarded him an iron certificate of mercy and a "virtuous rule" stele.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，僖宗崩。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the third month, Emperor Xizong of Tang died.
translations.idiomatic: On the third month's gengzi day, Emperor Xizong of Tang died.

sentences.zh: 天雄軍亂，囚其節度使樂彥貞。

translations.literal: The Tianxiong army mutinied and imprisoned its military governor Yue Yanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianxiong garrison mutinied and seized its governor Yue Yanzhen.

sentences.zh: 其子相州刺史從訓攻魏，來乞兵。

translations.literal: His son Yue Congxun, prefect of Xiang, attacked Wei and came begging for troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congxun, governor of Xiangzhou, besieged Wei and asked the Prince for soldiers.

sentences.zh: 遣硃珍助從訓攻魏。

translations.literal: He sent Zhu Zhen to help Congxun attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince sent Zhu Zhen to aid the assault on Wei.

sentences.zh: 而魏軍殺彥貞，從訓戰死，魏人立羅弘信，珍乃還。

translations.literal: The Wei troops killed Yanzhen; Congxun died in battle; the Wei people set up Luo Hongxin, and Zhen returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's soldiers killed Yanzhen. Congxun fell in the fighting. They elevated Luo Hongxin, and Zhen withdrew.

sentences.zh: 張全義取河陽，逐李罕之。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyi took Heyang and drove out Li Hanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi seized Heyang and expelled Li Hanzhi.

sentences.zh: 罕之奔於河東。

translations.literal: Hanzhi fled to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi ran to Li Keyong in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣兵圍河陽，全義來求救，遣丁會、牛存節救之，擊敗河東兵於沇河。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent troops to besiege Heyang; Quanyi came begging rescue; he sent Ding Hui and Niu Cunjie to save him and defeated the Hedong troops at the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong besieged Heyang. Quanyi appealed to the Prince, who sent Ding Hui and Niu Cunjie; they broke the Hedong army at the Si River.

sentences.zh: 五月，行營討蔡州，圍之百餘日，不克。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the campaign army besieged Cai Prefecture for more than a hundred days without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the coalition laid siege to Caizhou for over a hundred days and could not crack it.

sentences.zh: 是時，時溥已為東南面都統，又以王統行營，而溥猶稱都統。

translations.literal: By then Shi Pu was already overall commander of the southeast, and the Prince was made overall commander of the campaign army, yet Pu still called himself overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu still styled himself supreme commander of the southeast even though the Prince now headed the field army—and Pu kept the grand title anyway.

sentences.zh: 王乃上書，論溥討蔡無功而不落都統，且欲激怒溥以起兵端。

translations.literal: The Prince then memorialized the throne, arguing that Pu had achieved nothing against Cai yet would not yield the overall command, and also wishing to provoke Pu into opening hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince petitioned the court: Pu had failed at Caizhou but refused to step down—and he meant to goad Pu into war.

sentences.zh: 初，高駢死，淮南亂，楚州刺史劉瓚來奔，納之，及王兵攻蔡不克，還，欲攻徐，乃遣硃珍將兵數千以東，聲言送瓚還楚州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gao Pian died, Huainan fell into disorder; Liu Zan, prefect of Chuzhou, came fleeing in submission, and he received him; when the Prince's troops could not take Cai and returned, he wished to attack Xu, and sent Zhu Zhen east with several thousand men, publicly claiming he was escorting Zan back to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Pian's death Huainan had torn itself apart. Chuzhou's Liu Zan had fled to the Prince for protection. When the siege of Cai failed, he turned on Xuzhou, sending Zhu Zhen east with a few thousand men under the cover of returning Zan home.

sentences.zh: 溥怒論己，又聞珍以兵來，果出兵拒之。

translations.literal: Pu was enraged at the accusations against him, and hearing that Zhen was coming with troops, he indeed sent troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Furious at the memorial and hearing Zhen was marching, Pu met force with force.

sentences.zh: 珍戰于吳康，大敗之，取其豐、蕭二縣。

translations.literal: Zhen fought at Wukang, routed him, and took the two counties of Feng and Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: At Wukang, Zhen smashed Pu and seized Feng and Xiao counties.

sentences.zh: 遂攻宿州，下之。

translations.literal: He then attacked Suzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He took Suzhou next.

sentences.zh: 珍屯蕭縣，別遣龐師古攻徐州。

translations.literal: Zhen camped at Xiao County and separately sent Pang Shigu to attack Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen held Xiaoxian while Pang Shigu pressed Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年正月，師古敗溥于呂梁。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Longji, Shigu defeated Pu at Lüliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the Longji reign (889), Shigu beat Pu at Lüliang.

sentences.zh: 淮西牙將申叢執秦宗權，折其足，將檻送京師；

translations.literal: A Huainan guard officer, Shen Cong, seized Qin Zongquan, broke his legs, and was about to send him in a cage to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Cong, an officer under Zongquan, seized his master, broke his legs, and prepared to cage him for Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 別將郭璠殺叢，篡宗權以來獻。

translations.literal: another officer, Guo Fan, killed Cong and usurped Zongquan to bring him in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: another officer, Guo Fan, murdered Cong and delivered Zongquan himself.

sentences.zh: 王遣行軍司馬李璠獻俘于京師，表郭璠淮西留後。

translations.literal: The Prince sent his campaign secretary Li Fan to present the captive at the capital and memorialized to make Guo Fan acting governor of Huainan West.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince sent Li Fan to present the prisoner in Chang'an and asked that Guo Fan be left in charge of Huainan West.

sentences.zh: 三月，天子封王為東平王。

translations.literal: In the third month the Son of Heaven enfeoffed the Prince as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court made him Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 七月，硃珍殺李唐賓，王如蕭縣，執珍殺之，遂攻徐州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zhu Zhen killed Li Tangbin; the Prince went to Xiao County, seized Zhen and executed him, then attacked Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhu Zhen murdered Li Tangbin. The Prince rode to Xiaoxian, arrested Zhen, and had him killed, then marched on Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，大雨，水，不能軍而旋。

translations.literal: In winter great rains flooded the land; unable to keep the army in the field, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Winter floods drowned the campaign; he pulled the army back.

sentences.zh: 初，黃巢敗走，李克用追之，至於冤朐，不及而旋。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huang Chao was beaten and fled, Li Keyong pursued him to Yuanqu but could not catch up and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao had fled east, Li Keyong chased him as far as Yuanqu, gave up, and turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 過汴，駐軍於北郊，王邀克用置酒上源驛，夜以兵攻之。

translations.literal: Passing Bian he encamped in the northern suburbs; the Prince invited Keyong to wine at the Shangyuan post station and attacked him with troops by night.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Bian he camped north of the city. The Prince invited him to dinner at Shangyuan Post—and ambushed him that night.

sentences.zh: 克用逾城而免，訟其事于京師，天子知曲在汴而和解之。

translations.literal: Keyong climbed over the wall and escaped; he lodged a complaint at the capital; the Son of Heaven knew Bian was in the wrong and reconciled them.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong scaled the wall and lived. He appealed to the court. The emperor knew Bian was at fault and forced a truce.

sentences.zh: 至是，宰相張浚私與汴交，王厚之以賂，浚為汴請伐河東。

translations.literal: By now the chief minister Zhang Jun was privately allied with Bian; the Prince lavished bribes on him, and Jun asked Bian's sake for a campaign against Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhang Jun was now in Bian's pocket. The Prince bought him lavishly, and Jun petitioned for war on Hedong.

sentences.zh: 唐諸大臣皆以為不可興師。

translations.literal: The great ministers of Tang all held that one should not raise armies.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the Tang cabinet opposed war.

sentences.zh: 浚挾汴力，請益堅。

translations.literal: Jun, relying on Bian's strength, pressed his request all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Backed by Bian's power, Jun only pushed harder.

sentences.zh: 天子不得已，許之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had no choice and consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor yielded.

sentences.zh: 五月，以浚為太原四面行營都統，王為東南面招討使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jun was made overall commander of the four-sided campaign against Taiyuan, and the Prince was made southeastern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jun became supreme commander against Taiyuan; the Prince was named southeastern commissioner.

sentences.zh: 然王不親兵，以兵三千屬浚而已。

translations.literal: Yet the Prince did not lead troops in person—he only assigned three thousand men to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince stayed home, lending Jun a mere three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 浚屯于陰地。

translations.literal: Jun encamped at Yindi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun camped at Yindi.

sentences.zh: 河東叛將馮霸殺潞州守將李克恭來降，遣葛從周入潞州。

translations.literal: A Hedong defector, Feng Ba, killed the Lu Prefecture garrison commander Li Ke Gong and came to surrender; he sent Ge Congzhou into Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba, a Hedong turncoat, killed Lu's commander Li Kegong and defected. The Prince sent Ge Congzhou to hold Lu.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣康君立攻之，從周走河陽。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent Kang Junli to attack; Congzhou fled to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Kang Junli to retake the city. Congzhou ran to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，王如河陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Prince went to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Prince marched to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 十月，天子以王兼宣義軍節度使，遂如滑州，假道于魏，以攻河東，且責其軍須，亦所以怒魏為兵端也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Son of Heaven made Quanzhong concurrently military governor of the Xuanyi army; he then went to Huazhou, passed through Wei on his way to attack Hedong, and also to demand his army's supplies—thereby also to provoke Wei into opening hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court gave Quanzhong the Xuanyi command as well. He marched to Huazhou, crossed Wei to strike Hedong, and demanded grain from the Wei garrison—partly to pick a fight.

sentences.zh: 魏人果以謂非兵所當出，而辭以糧乏，皆不許。

translations.literal: The people of Wei indeed held that such troops ought not to come their way; they all refused on the plea of scarce grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commanders said his route was wrong and pleaded empty granaries. Every request was refused.

sentences.zh: 於是攻魏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He turned on Wei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，張浚之師大敗于陰地。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhang Jun's army was utterly defeated at Yindi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhang Jun's army was smashed at Yindi.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，王及魏人戰于內黃，大敗之，屠故元城，羅弘信來送款。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Quanzhong fought the Wei people at Neihuang, utterly defeated them, slaughtered the old Yuan city, and Luo Hongxin came to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Quanzhong met the Wei army at Neihuang, crushed it, sacked old Yuancheng, and Luo Hongxin submitted.

sentences.zh: 十月，克宿州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he took Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he seized Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，曹州將郭紹賓殺其刺史郭饒來降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Guo Shaobin, a general of Cao Prefecture, killed its prefect Guo Rao and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Guo Shaobin, an officer of Caozhou, murdered the prefect Guo Rao and defected.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁會敗硃瑾于金鄉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Ding Hui defeated Zhu Jin at Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Ding Hui routed Zhu Jin at Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 景福元年二月，攻鄆州，前軍硃友裕敗于斗門，王軍後至，又敗而還。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jingfu he attacked Yan Prefecture; the vanguard Zhu Youyu was defeated at Dou Gate; Quanzhong's army came up afterward, was defeated again, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jingfu 1 (892) he besieged Yanzhou. Zhu Youyu's vanguard lost at Dou Gate; when Quanzhong came up with the main body he was beaten again and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 冬，友裕取濮州，遂攻徐州。

translations.literal: In winter Youyu took Pu Prefecture, then attacked Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Youyu took Puzhou and pressed Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，龐師古克徐州，殺時溥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year Pang Shigu took Xuzhou and killed Shi Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Pang Shigu captured Xuzhou and killed Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 王如徐州，以師古為留後，遂攻兗、鄆。

translations.literal: Quanzhong went to Xuzhou, left Shigu as acting prefect, then attacked Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong went to Xuzhou, left Shigu as garrison commander, and marched on Yan and Yun prefectures.

sentences.zh: 光化元年三月，天子以王兼天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua the Son of Heaven made Quanzhong concurrently military governor of the Tianping army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guanghua 1 (898) the court added the Tianping command to Quanzhong's titles.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣葛從周攻晉之山東，取邢、洺、磁三州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he sent Ge Congzhou to attack Hedong's Shandong region and took Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he sent Ge Congzhou into Hedong's Shandong districts and seized Xing, Ming, and Ci.

sentences.zh: 襄州趙匡凝自其父德諲時來附，匡凝又與楊行密、李克用通，而其事泄。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture had submitted since his father Dezhao's time; Kuangning again communicated with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the matter was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou had been a vassal since his father Dezhao's day. He was now in touch with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the traffic was discovered.

sentences.zh: 七月，遣氏叔琮、康懷英攻匡凝，取其泌、隨、鄧三州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying to attack Kuangning and took his Mi, Sui, and Deng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying against Kuangning and took Mi, Sui, and Deng.

sentences.zh: 匡凝請和，乃止。

translations.literal: Kuangning sued for peace, and the attack stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning sued for peace and the campaign ended.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李罕之以潞州來降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Li Hanzhi surrendered Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Hanzhi handed Luzhou over.

sentences.zh: 二年，幽州劉仁恭攻魏，羅紹威來求救。

translations.literal: In the second year Liu Rengong of Youzhou attacked Wei; Luo Shaowei came to beg rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Liu Rengong of Youzhou struck Wei, and Luo Shaowei called for help.

sentences.zh: 王救魏，敗仁恭于內黃。

translations.literal: Quanzhong rescued Wei and defeated Rengong at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong relieved Wei and beat Rengong at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣氏叔琮攻晉太原，不克。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he sent Shi Shuzong to attack Taiyuan of Jin but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he sent Shi Shuzong against Taiyuan; the city held.

sentences.zh: 七月，李克用取澤、潞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Li Keyong took Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Li Keyong recovered Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，保義軍亂，殺其節度使王珙，推其牙將李璠為留後，其將硃簡殺璠來降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Baoyi army mutinied, killed its military governor Wang Gong, pushed its gate officer Li Fan as acting prefect; his officer Zhu Jian killed Fan and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Baoyi garrison murdered its governor Wang Gong and made a gate officer, Li Fan, acting commander. Zhu Jian killed Fan and defected.

sentences.zh: 以簡為保義軍節度使。

translations.literal: He made Jian military governor of Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong installed Jian as governor of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，遣葛從周攻劉仁恭之滄州，取其德州，及仁恭戰於老鴉堤，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou to attack Liu Rengong's Cangzhou, took his Dezhou, fought Rengong at Laoya Embankment, and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou against Liu Rengong's Cangzhou, seized Dezhou, and shattered Rengong at Laoya Embankment.

sentences.zh: 八月，晉取洺州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Jin took Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Hedong retook Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王如洺州，復取之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong went to Ming Prefecture and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong marched to Mingzhou and won it back.

sentences.zh: 是時，鎮、定皆附于晉。

translations.literal: At this time Zhen and Ding were both attached to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhenzhou and Dingzhou both stood with Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遂攻鎮州，破臨城，王鎔來送款。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked Zhen Prefecture, broke Lincheng, and Wang Rong came to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Zhenzhou, stormed Lincheng, and Wang Rong submitted.

sentences.zh: 進攻定州，王郜奔于晉，其將王處直以定州降。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Ding Prefecture, Wang Gao fled to Jin; his officer Wang Chuzhi surrendered Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing Dingzhou, Wang Gao fled to Hedong; his general Wang Chuzhi surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 自劉季述等已誅，宰相崔胤外與梁交，欲假梁兵盡誅宦者。

translations.literal: Since Liu Jishu and the others had been executed, chief minister Cui Yin externally allied with Liang and wished to borrow Liang troops to execute all the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jishu and his fellows were dead, chief minister Cui Yin courted Liang from outside the palace and wanted Liang soldiers to wipe out every eunuch.

sentences.zh: 而鳳翔李茂貞、邠甯王行瑜等，皆遣子弟以精兵宿衛天子，宦官韓全誨等亦因恃以為助。

translations.literal: But Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Binning, and the rest all sent younger kinsmen with elite troops to guard the Son of Heaven at court; eunuch Han Quanhui and the others also relied on them as support.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Binning, and others posted sons and nephews with crack troops to guard the emperor. Han Quanhui and the palace eunuchs leaned on them in turn.

sentences.zh: 天子與胤計事，宦者屬耳，頗聞之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven and Yin discussed affairs, the eunuchs leaned close and heard much of it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor and Yin plotted, eunuchs pressed close enough to overhear.

sentences.zh: 乃選美女，內之宮中，陰令伺察其實。

translations.literal: They then selected beautiful women and placed them within the palace, secretly ordering them to spy out the truth.
translations.idiomatic: They planted beautiful women in the inner quarters and told them to learn what was really being said.

sentences.zh: 久之，果得胤奏謀所以誅宦者之說，全誨等大懼，日夜相與涕泣，思圖胤以求全。

translations.literal: After a long while they indeed obtained Yin's memorial setting forth the plan to execute the eunuchs; Quanhui and the others were greatly afraid; night and day together they wept, scheming to strike at Yin in order to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In time they got hold of Yin's memorial on killing the eunuchs. Quanhui and his party were terrified; day and night they wept together and plotted to destroy Yin before he destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 胤知謀泄，事急，即矯為制，召梁兵入誅宦者。

translations.literal: Yin knew the plot was leaked; matters were urgent; he immediately forged an edict summoning Liang troops to enter and execute the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Yin knew the secret was out. In desperation he forged an edict calling Liang troops to the capital to slaughter the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 十月，王以宣武、宣義、天平、護國兵七萬，至於河中，取同州，遂攻華州，韓建出降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Quanzhong led seventy thousand troops of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo to Hezhong, took Tong Prefecture, then attacked Huazhou; Han Jian came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Quanzhong marched seventy thousand men from Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo to Hezhong, seized Tongzhou, then took Huazhou when Han Jian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 全誨等聞梁王兵且至，即以岐、邠宿衛兵劫天子奔于鳳翔。

translations.literal: When Quanhui and the others heard Liang Wang's troops were about to arrive, they took the Fengxiang and Binning palace guards and seized the Son of Heaven, fleeing to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Quanzhong's army was near, Quanhui and the rest used the Fengxiang and Binning guards to seize the emperor and flee to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 王乃上書言胤所以召之之意。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then memorialized, explaining the meaning of why Yin had summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong memorialized the throne, explaining why Yin had called him west.

sentences.zh: 天子怒，罷胤相，責授工部尚書，詔梁兵還鎮。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was angry, dismissed Yin from the chief ministership, demoted him to Minister of Works, and ordered the Liang troops to return to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. He stripped Yin of the chancellorship, made him Minister of Works, and ordered the Liang army home.

sentences.zh: 王引兵去，攻邠州，屯于三原。

translations.literal: Quanzhong withdrew his troops, attacked Bin Prefecture, and encamped at Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong pulled back, struck Binzhou, and camped at Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 邠州節度使楊崇本以邠、甯、慶、衍四州降。

translations.literal: Bin military governor Yang Chongben surrendered Bin, Ning, Qing, and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongben of Binning surrendered Bin, Ning, Qing, and Yan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 崔胤奔于華州。

translations.literal: Cui Yin fled to Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin fled to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 二年春，王退軍於河中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Quanzhong withdrew his army to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Quanzhong drew his army back to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 晉攻晉、絳。

translations.literal: Jin attacked Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong forces attacked Jinzhou and Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣硃友甯擊敗晉軍于蒲縣，取汾、慈、隰，遂圍太原，不克而還，汾、慈、隰復入于晉。

translations.literal: He sent Zhu Youning to defeat the Jin army at Pu County, took Fen, Ci, and Xi, then besieged Taiyuan but could not take it and returned; Fen, Ci, and Xi again fell to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhu Youning to smash the Hedong army at Puxian, took Fen, Ci, and Xi, then besieged Taiyuan without success. On the march home Fen, Ci, and Xi slipped back to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 四月，友甯引兵西，至興平，及李茂貞戰於武功，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Youning led troops west to Xingping and at Wugong fought Li Maozhen, utterly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Youning marched west to Xingping and routed Li Maozhen at Wugong.

sentences.zh: 王兵犯鳳翔，茂貞數出戰，輒敗，遂圍之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong's troops assailed Fengxiang; Maozhen came out to fight several times, was repeatedly defeated, and was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong pressed Fengxiang. Maozhen sallied again and again, lost every time, and was penned in the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月，鄜坊李周彝以兵救鳳翔，王遣孔勍襲鄜州，虜周彝之族，徙於河中，周彝乃降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Li Zhouyi of Yan-Fang led troops to rescue Fengxiang; Quanzhong sent Kong Xun to raid Yan Prefecture, captured Zhouyi's clan, moved them to Hezhong, and Zhouyi then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Zhouyi of Yan-Fang marched to relieve Fengxiang. Quanzhong sent Kong Xun to strike Yanzhou, seized Zhouyi's family, relocated them to Hezhong, and Zhouyi submitted.

sentences.zh: 是時，岐兵屢敗，而圍久，城中食盡，自天子至後宮，皆凍餒。

translations.literal: At this time the Fengxiang troops were repeatedly defeated, the siege was long, food in the city was exhausted, and from the Son of Heaven down to the inner palace all suffered cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang's armies kept losing, the siege dragged on, and provisions ran out. From the emperor to the inner palace, everyone froze and starved.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，茂貞殺韓全誨等二十人，囊其首，示梁軍，約出天子以為解。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Maozhen killed Quanhui and twenty others, bagged their heads, displayed them to the Liang army, and agreed to release the Son of Heaven as the price of relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Maozhen executed Quanhui and twenty companions, packed their heads in sacks, showed them to the Liang camp, and offered to hand over the emperor to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 甲子，天子出幸梁軍。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day the Son of Heaven went out to visit the Liang army.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi the emperor walked out to the Liang lines.

sentences.zh: 遣使者馳召崔胤，胤托疾不至。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy at full gallop to summon Cui Yin; Yin pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Riders were sent at full gallop to fetch Cui Yin. Yin claimed illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 王使人戲胤曰：「吾未識天子，懼其非是，子來為我辨之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong had someone jest to Yin: "I do not know the Son of Heaven and fear he may not be the real one—come distinguish him for me.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Yin a mocking message: "I have never met the Son of Heaven and cannot be sure this is he. Come tell me if he is real.

sentences.zh: 」天子還至興平，胤率百官奉迎。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven returned to Xingping; Yin led the hundred officials to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor reached Xingping, Yin led the whole court out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 王自為天子執轡，且泣且行，行十餘里，止之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong himself held the Son of Heaven's reins, weeping as he walked more than ten li, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong took the imperial bridle himself and walked beside the carriage for more than ten li, weeping the whole way before he let go.

sentences.zh: 人見者，咸以為忠。

translations.literal: Those who saw it all considered it loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers took it for the height of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 己巳，天子至自鳳翔，素服哭於太廟而後入，殺宦者七百餘人。

translations.literal: On the jisi day the Son of Heaven arrived from Fengxiang, in plain robes wept at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and then entered, and killed more than seven hundred eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi the emperor came down from Fengxiang, mourned at the ancestral temple in undyed robes, entered the palace, and put more than seven hundred eunuchs to death.

sentences.zh: 二月甲戌，天子賜王「回天再造竭忠守正功臣」，以輝王祚為諸道兵馬元帥，王為副元帥。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day jiaxu of the second month the Son of Heaven granted Quanzhong the title "Merit subject who turns back heaven and remakes, exhausts loyalty and upholds rectitude"; he made Prince Huiwang commander of all circuit armies and Quanzhong deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu in the second month the emperor gave Quanzhong the title "Merit subject who turns back heaven and remakes, exhausts loyalty and upholds rectitude," named Prince Hui commander of all circuit armies, and made Quanzhong his deputy.

sentences.zh: 王乃留子友倫為護駕指揮使，以為天子衛，引兵東歸。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then left his son Youlun as protector-escort commander to guard the Son of Heaven and led his troops east in return.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong left his son Youlun as protector of the imperial escort to guard the emperor and marched east.

sentences.zh: 天子餞于延喜樓，賜《楊柳枝》五曲。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven gave a farewell feast at Yanxi Tower and granted five airs of "Willow Branch."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave a farewell banquet at Yanxi Tower and bestowed five performances of "Willow Branch."

sentences.zh: 初，梁兵已西，青州王師範遣其將劉鄩襲據梁兗州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liang troops had gone west, Wang Shifan of Qingzhou sent his general Liu Yun to strike and seize Liang's Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While the Liang army was still in the west, Wang Shifan of Qingzhou sent Liu Yun to raid and seize Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 王已還梁，四月，如鄆州，遣硃友甯攻青州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong had already returned to Liang; in the fourth month he went to Yanzhou and sent Zhu Youning to attack Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was back in the east. In the fourth month he went to Yanzhou and sent Zhu Youning against Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 師範敗之于石樓，友甯死。

translations.literal: Shifan defeated him at Shilou; Youning died.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan beat him at Shilou and Youning was killed.

sentences.zh: 九月，楊師厚敗青人於臨朐，取其棣州，師範以青州降，而鄩亦降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Yang Shihou defeated the Qingzhou men at Linqu, took their Di Prefecture; Shifan surrendered Qingzhou, and Yun also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yang Shihou routed the Qingzhou army at Linqu and took Di Prefecture. Shifan surrendered Qingzhou, and Liu Yun came over as well.

sentences.zh: 友倫擊鞠，墜馬死。

translations.literal: Youlun was playing cuju, fell from his horse and died.
translations.idiomatic: Youlun fell from his horse during a cuju match and died.

sentences.zh: 王怒，以為崔胤殺之，遣硃友謙殺胤于京師。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was angry, believing Cui Yin had killed him, and sent Zhu Youqian to kill Yin at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong blamed Cui Yin for the death and sent Zhu Youqian to murder Yin in the capital.

sentences.zh: 其與友倫擊鞠者，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Those who had been playing cuju with Youlun were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who had been on the field with Youlun was executed.

sentences.zh: 自天子奔華州，王請遷都洛陽，雖不許，而王命河南張全義修洛陽宮以待。

translations.literal: From the time the Son of Heaven fled to Huazhou, Quanzhong had asked to move the capital to Luoyang; though not permitted, he ordered Zhang Quanyi of Henan to repair Luoyang Palace to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the emperor had fled to Huazhou, Quanzhong had pressed to move the court to Luoyang. The request was denied, but he told Zhang Quanyi of Henan to rebuild the Luoyang palaces and wait.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年正月，王如河中，遣牙將寇彥卿如京師，請遷都洛陽，並徙長安居人以東。

translations.literal: In the first month of Tainyou 1 Quanzhong went to Hezhong and sent his gate officer Kou Yanqing to the capital to request moving the capital to Luoyang and also to relocate the people of Chang'an eastward.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tainyou 1 (904) Quanzhong went to Hezhong and sent his gate officer Kou Yanqing to Chang'an to demand the move to Luoyang and the resettlement of the western capital's population.

sentences.zh: 天子行至陝州，王朝於行在，先如東都。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven traveled to Shaan Prefecture, Quanzhong paid court at the mobile court and went first to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Shaanzhou, Quanzhong attended the traveling court and went on ahead to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是時，六軍諸衛兵已散亡，其從以東者，小黃門十數人，打球供奉、內園小兒等二百餘人。

translations.literal: At this time the Six Armies and various guards' troops had scattered and fled; those who followed east were a dozen or so junior yellow-gate eunuchs, ball-game attendants, inner-garden boys, and the like—more than two hundred persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies and palace guards had melted away. Only a dozen junior eunuchs, ball attendants, and inner-garden boys—barely two hundred souls—followed the emperor east.

sentences.zh: 行至谷水，王教醫官許昭遠告其謀亂，悉殺而代之，然後以聞。

translations.literal: When they reached Gu River, Quanzhong had the medical officer Xu Zhaoyuan report their plot to rebel; he killed them all and replaced them, and only then reported it.
translations.idiomatic: At Gu River Quanzhong had the physician Xu Zhaoyuan accuse them of plotting revolt, killed every one, slipped in Liang men, and only then informed the emperor.

sentences.zh: 由是天子左右皆梁人矣。

translations.literal: From this the Son of Heaven's attendants were all men of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After that every face around the emperor was a Liang man.

sentences.zh: 四月甲辰，天子至自西都。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day jiachen of the fourth month the Son of Heaven arrived from the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the fourth month the emperor entered Luoyang from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉王李克用、岐王李茂貞、楚王趙匡凝、蜀王王建、吳王楊行密聞梁遷天子洛陽，皆欲舉兵討梁，王大懼。

translations.literal: At this time Jin Prince Li Keyong, Fengxiang Prince Li Maozhen, Chu Prince Zhao Kuangning, Shu Prince Wang Jian, and Wu Prince Yang Xingmi, hearing that Liang was moving the Son of Heaven to Luoyang, all wished to raise troops to punish Liang; Quanzhong was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Jin, Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Zhao Kuangning of Chu, Wang Jian of Shu, and Yang Xingmi of Wu all talked of marching on Liang once they heard the emperor was being dragged to Luoyang. Quanzhong was terrified.

sentences.zh: 六月，楊崇本復附於岐。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yang Chongben again submitted to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yang Chongben went back to Maozhen's side.

sentences.zh: 王乃以兵如河中，聲言攻崇本，遣硃友恭、氏叔琮、蔣玄暉等行弑，昭宗崩。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then led troops to Hezhong, proclaiming that he would attack Chongben, and dispatched Zhu Yougong, Shi Shuzong, Jiang Xuanhui, and others to carry out assassination—Emperor Zhaozong died.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong marched on Hezhong, claiming he would punish Chongben, while Zhu Yougong, Shi Shuzong, Jiang Xuanhui, and others carried out the murder. Emperor Zhaozong was dead.

sentences.zh: 十月，王朝于京師，殺硃友恭、氏叔琮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Quanzhong paid court at the capital and killed Zhu Yougong and Shi Shuzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Quanzhong appeared at court and executed Zhu Yougong and Shi Shuzong as scapegoats.

sentences.zh: 十一月，攻淮南，取其光州，攻壽州，不克而旋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he attacked Huainan, took its Guang Prefecture, attacked Shou Prefecture, could not take it, and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he campaigned in Huainan, took Guangzhou, failed at Shouzhou, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，遣蔣玄暉殺德王裕等九王于九曲池。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year he sent Jiang Xuanhui to kill the nine princes including De Wang Yu at Jiuchi Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year he had Jiang Xuanhui drown nine princes, including De Wang Yu, in Jiuchi Pool.

sentences.zh: 六月，殺司空裴贄等百餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he killed more than a hundred persons including Sikong Pei Zan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he slaughtered more than a hundred officials, among them Sikong Pei Zan.

sentences.zh: 七月，天子使來，賜王「迎鑾紀功碑」。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Son of Heaven sent envoys granting Quanzhong the "Stele Inscribing Merit in Welcoming the Imperial Carriage."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the court sent envoys with the stele title "Inscribing Merit in Welcoming the Imperial Carriage."

sentences.zh: 王欲代唐，使人諭諸鎮，襄州趙匡凝以為不可。

translations.literal: Quanzhong wished to replace Tang and sent men to inform the various circuits; Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong meant to take the throne and sounded out the provinces. Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou said no.

sentences.zh: 遣楊師厚攻之，取其唐、鄧、復、郢、隨、均、房七州。

translations.literal: He sent Yang Shihou to attack him and took his seven prefectures Tang, Deng, Fu, Ying, Sui, Jun, and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yang Shihou against him and stripped away Tang, Deng, Fu, Ying, Sui, Jun, and Fang—seven prefectures in all.

sentences.zh: 王如襄州，軍於漢北。

translations.literal: Quanzhong went to Xiang Prefecture and encamped north of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong advanced to Xiangzhou and camped on the north bank of the Han.

sentences.zh: 九月，師厚破襄州，匡凝奔於淮南。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shihou broke Xiang Prefecture; Kuangning fled to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shihou stormed Xiangzhou and Kuangning fled to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 師厚取荊南，荊南留後趙匡明奔於蜀。

translations.literal: Shihou took Jingnan; Jingnan acting prefect Zhao Kuangming fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou seized Jingnan. Its acting prefect Zhao Kuangming ran to Shu.

sentences.zh: 遂出光州，以攻壽州，不克。

translations.literal: He then moved out of Guang Prefecture to attack Shou Prefecture but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He marched from Guangzhou against Shouzhou but failed again.

sentences.zh: 天子卜祀天于南郊，王怒，以為蔣玄暉等欲祈天以延唐。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven divined for a suburban sacrifice at the southern suburb; Quanzhong was angry, believing Jiang Xuanhui and the others wished to pray to Heaven to prolong Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cast lots for a southern suburban rite. Quanzhong raged, convinced that Jiang Xuanhui and his circle meant to pray Heaven into keeping Tang alive.

sentences.zh: 天子懼，改卜郊。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was afraid and changed the date of the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor postponed the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛巳，天子封王為魏王、相國，總百揆。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day xinsi of the eleventh month the Son of Heaven enfeoffed Quanzhong as Prince of Wei and Chancellor of State, directing all affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the eleventh month the emperor made Quanzhong Prince of Wei and Chancellor of State with authority over all government.

sentences.zh: 以宣武、宣義、天平、護國、天雄、武順、佑國、河陽、義武、昭義、武寧、保義、忠義、武昭、武定、泰甯、平盧、匡國、鎮國、荊南、忠武二十一軍為魏國，備九錫。

translations.literal: He made twenty-one armies including Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo, Tianxiong, Wushun, Youguo, Heyang, Yiwu, Zhaoyi, Wuning, Baoyi, Zhongyi, Wuzhao, Wuding, Taining, Pinglu, Kuangguo, Zhenguo, Jingnan, and Zhongwu into the state of Wei, with the full nine bestowments prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one commands—from Xuanwu and Xuanyi to Zhongwu—were bundled into a Wei state for him, and the full nine bestowments were readied.

sentences.zh: 王怒，不受。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was angry and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong refused in fury.

sentences.zh: 十二月，天子以王為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Son of Heaven made Quanzhong commander of all forces under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor named him commander of all armies under heaven.

sentences.zh: 王益怒，遣人告樞密使蔣玄暉與何太后私通，殺玄暉而焚之，遂弑太后于積善宮。

translations.literal: Quanzhong grew still angrier; he sent men to accuse Grand Councilor Jiang Xuanhui of illicit relations with Empress Dowager He, killed Xuanhui and burned him, then murdered the empress dowager at Jishan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's rage only grew. He charged Grand Councilor Jiang Xuanhui with sleeping with Empress Dowager He, killed and burned him, then murdered the empress dowager in Jishan Palace.

sentences.zh: 又殺宰相柳璨，太常卿張延範車裂以徇。

translations.literal: He also killed chief minister Liu Can and had Minister of Rites Zhang Yanfan dismembered by cart and paraded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He executed chief minister Liu Can and had Minister of Rites Zhang Yanfan torn apart by carts and displayed in the streets.

sentences.zh: 天子詔以太后故停郊。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued an edict stopping the suburban sacrifice on account of the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor announced that the suburban rites were canceled because of the empress dowager's death.

sentences.zh: 三年春，魏州羅紹威謀殺其牙軍，來假兵以虞變，王為發兵北攻劉仁恭之滄州，兵過魏而紹威已殺牙軍，其兵之在外者果皆叛，據貝、衛、澶、博州，王以兵悉殺之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Luo Shaowei of Weizhou plotted to kill his gate army and came to borrow troops to guard against trouble; Quanzhong raised troops north to attack Liu Rengong's Cangzhou; when the army passed Wei, Shaowei had already killed the gate army; those of his troops who were outside indeed all rebelled, occupying Bei, Wei, Chan, and Bo prefectures; Quanzhong led troops and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Luo Shaowei of Weizhou planned to wipe out his own gate troops and asked Quanzhong for soldiers to hold the line. Quanzhong marched north against Liu Rengong's Cangzhou. Passing through Wei he found Shaowei had already slaughtered the gate army, but the detachments still in the field rose in Bei, Wei, Chan, and Bo. Quanzhong hunted every mutineer down and killed them.

sentences.zh: 遂攻滄州，軍于長蘆。

translations.literal: He then attacked Cangzhou and encamped at Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Cangzhou and camped at Changlu.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭求救于晉。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong sought rescue from Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong appealed to Jin for help.

sentences.zh: 晉人取潞州，王乃旋軍。

translations.literal: The Jin forces took Luzhou, and the Prince thereupon turned his army back.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin seized Luzhou, Quanzhong wheeled his army about and withdrew.
